To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
women's knowledge of the age-related risk of breast cancer is poor.
women's knowledge that breast cancer risk increases with age was very low and that the majority of women believed that the risk of the disease was the same for all women.
women's knowledge of breast cancer risk is poor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the knowledge that women have regarding breast cancer risk.
the knowledge of women about breast cancer and its risk factors.
the role of knowledge in the development and maintenance of beliefs about the risk of breast disease and the implications for screening.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the risk of developing breast cancer increases with increasing age.
the risk of developing breast cancer is not known to vary with age.
the majority of the women in this survey were unaware that their risk of developing breast cancer increased with age.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that women's knowledge of breast cancer risk is poor.
the majority of women do not know that the risk increases with age and therefore are not likely to be able to inform their health seeking behaviour.
we need to do more to inform women of the increased risk of breast cancer with age.
The main takeaway from our work is that
women need to be informed about the risk of breast-cancer with age.
the public need to be better informed about the age-related increase in the risk of breast and other cancers.
women need to know that their risk of breast cancer is increased with age.
